enumeration_state.required_replacement: W0-B must populate a content-addressed SourceModel-derived package-manifest section while retaining these reviewed resolution rules.
enumeration_state.statement: No package enumeration has run for this registry.

fail_closed_resolution.applies_to: every SourceModel package and every declared external runtime dependency at the upstream pin
failure_conditions: No scope rule matches a resolution subject in any declared domain.
More than one matching rule has the highest specificity rank.
A selected rule has a disposition outside the exact disposition_vocabulary.
A ported crate maps to a selected EXCLUDE or CONSUME rule.
fail_closed_resolution.matching: All selectors within a rule match conjunctively. A package resolves to exactly one selected rule: the matching rule with the highest specificity_rank. Equal highest ranks are an error.
fail_closed_resolution.result: A failed resolution blocks package admission, generation, and activation.

rules.rationale: Generated upstream inputs are recorded as inputs or regenerated through the governed generator path; they are not handwritten port targets.
Third-party and vendored code retains its own provenance and is not first-party Kubernetes port scope.
Documentation and examples are not product package targets; their executable test cases remain subject to test accounting.
Packages excluded by the selected port platform or build tags are deferred only through an explicit SourceModel build-constraint classification.
In-tree legacy cloud providers are excluded from the owned port.
In-tree volume plugins are excluded; CSI drivers are consumed as external dependencies rather than ported plugins.
Dockershim residue is outside the target runtime model.
API groups older than pin minus three minors are excluded by lifecycle metadata, not by an unverified handwritten package list.
hack/** and k8s.io/code-generator are replaced by governed port-engine rules rather than ported as Kubernetes product packages.
etcd, containerd and CRI runtimes, CNI plugin binaries, CSI drivers, and CoreDNS remain external runtime dependencies rather than port targets.
API machinery and API types are core whole-of-Kubernetes A-prime port scope.
Client machinery, including REST, transport, discovery, informers, listers, workqueue, cache tooling, and leader election, is in scope.

Component base, apiserver, endpoints, storage and etcd integration, admission, authentication, authorization, audit, aggregation, API extensions, OpenAPI, kube-apiserver, scheduler, and controller manager are in scope.
Full A-prime includes kubelet and kube-proxy from program start; G3 is a fallback gate, not an exclusion.
kubectl is in the whole-of-Kubernetes A-prime scope.
The default disposition is PORT for buildable first-party Go packages at the pin, subject to higher-specificity scope rows.

test_accounting.rule: Every upstream test and dynamically generated table or subtest case associated with an admitted package must receive one executable, pin-versioned L0 disposition. Scope exclusion does not authorize skipping or deleting a test.
